articleTitle: Anti-friction bearing temperature rise for NEMA frame motors
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: The authors identify the location for monitoring the bearing temperature rises for NEMA frame, chemical industry, severe duty squirrel-cage induction motors. They then investigate the relationship between bearing temperature rise and the stator winding temperature rise. An overview of the types of most commonly used antifriction bearings, criteria for selection of such bearings, and factors affecting bearing life are also presented. It is found that bearing operating temperature is an important parameter in motor specifications. For optimum motor design, the bearing temperature specified should be consistent with the motor RPM and the winding temperature rise.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Evaluation of electrical hazards in AC low voltage systems
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: The safety of 600 V and below AC systems is discussed. Electrical hazard criteria based on tolerable step and touch voltages are established. The performance of circuit breakers and fuses with respect to electrical hazards are evaluated. Some design recommendations are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Parameter estimation for induction machines based on sensitivity analysis
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: A mathematical method is described for estimating the equivalent circuit parameters of induction machines from the most readily available performance characteristics. The method utilizes machine equations to estimate the parameters and then performs sensitivity analyses with respect to the circuit parameters to match the given performance characteristics. An example is included to illustrate how well the performance of the estimated model matches that of the actual machine.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: 480 volt corner grounded delta: friend or foe
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: A review is given of 480 V corner-grounded delta service for oil fields. It is found that, although this type of service is less expensive than solidly grounded wye service, 480 V corner-grounded delta service may not provide a safe working environment if used for oil-field service. The problems found include: dangerous step and touch potentials can exist; nonautomatic isolation and location of phase-to-ground shorts; ground currents objectionable to residents living in the area; ground potentials have been known to cause solid-state starters to start in the off position; lightning arrestor application may be unsatisfactory; AC interference to communication equipment; higher dielectric stress on two phases; and higher magnitudes of transient overvoltages.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Applying adjustable speed AC drives to cooling tower fans
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: An economic evaluation was performed to determine the potential annual savings achieved by using adjustable-speed AC drives on cooling tower fans. It was found that using any adjustable-speed drive technology to track the wet-bulb temperature throughout the year will result in an annual energy savings of 83% when compared with running the fans at full speed all the time. Pulsewidth modulation was found to be the optimum solution for efficiency, harmonic distortion feedback, and power-factor considerations. The digital drive also offered the control options necessary to successfully operate with two fans in parallel on one drive. These options included the capability for bypass starters, automatic transfer, and selectable fault condition responses. In addition to the energy savings offered by the digital drives, being able to adjust the speed of the fans would result in smoother plant operations due to constant water temperatures. The adjustable-speed drives also enable the fans to be soft started.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The application of a continuous leak detection system to pipelines and associated equipment
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: Some examples of leaks occurring in pipelines are considered, and an overview of classical leak detection systems and the engineering basis of a novel type of detector system are given. The hydrocarbon sensor system consists of an alarm module and sensing cable. This sensing cable provides distributed coverage by detecting leaks of most fuels and solvents at any point along its length. The cable can be used in lengths of up to 2 km with a resolution of approximately 1% of the length for leak detection. The simple electrical circuit is also described that locates and detects a leak anywhere along the length of the sensor.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Self-checking safety interlock system
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: A more reliable electrical self-checking interlock system is discussed that meets the desired goals of safety shutdown systems. The design, operating principles, and performance characteristics of the microprocessor-based, self-checking, safety interlock system are described. The system was designed and implemented in a large plant. The system has substantially improved safety and environmental control of the processes, in addition to its inherent advantages of process analysis and optimization over conventional systems. With some modification the system can be programmed to verify functionality of the final interlock elements for additional safety improvement.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The practice of ground differential relaying
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: The basic concepts are presented of ground differential protection for transformers and generators. Ground differential relaying provides fast and sensitive ground fault protection for wye-connected and ground electrical power equipment such as rotating generators or power transformers. Because it is a differential system, there is no need to incorporate undesirable time delay or to sacrifice sensitivity for the sake of system coordination. The authors first explain ground differential relaying for power transformers and generators, and then explain the ground differential scheme using a commercially available product type relay. Finally, they illustrate a method of current transformer selection that will help better implementation of the ground differential scheme.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Starting of large motors-methods and economics
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: The available starting methods are discussed for motors above 3000 hp, focusing on technical and economic aspects. The following schemes are discussed: direct online, reactor start, auto transformer start, capacitor start, capative transformer start, and frequency start. A review of the network conditions which favor a particular starting method is given. A guide is given for the selection of starting methods on the basis of type of driven equipment, network conditions, and cost.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The application of a 3500 HP variable frequency drive for pipeline pump control
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: The installation and use of a 3500 HP adjustable-speed drive on a crude-oil/natural-gas pipeline is described. The unit presented is a variable-frequency induction motor drive using gate turn-off thyristors. It increased the capacity of the pipeline from 130000 barrels/day to 185000 barrels/day.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Harmonics and technical barriers in adjustable speed drives
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: The presence of harmonics in both six-pulse and twelve-pulse converter systems is analyzed emphasising the differences between three-phase and six-phase machines in suppressing these harmonics. The effect of the use of harmonic filters and special transformer-winding arrangements in reducing harmonics is also discussed. Harmonics measurements for two actual installations are presented and analyzed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An illustration of harmonic suppression due to transformer connection-a simplified approach
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: A basic simplified mathematical explanation is provided for the harmonic suppression that can occur when transformer pairs servicing power system converter or rectifier loads are connected delta-delta on one unit and delta-wye on the other unit, such that a 30 degrees phase shift exists between transformer secondaries. The Fourier series is used to define the phasor quantities (relative magnitude) for each harmonic required to construct the current square wave. A relative phase angle is derived for each harmonic to complete the phasor. It is from these phasors (and the relationship of the connections for the transformer pair) that cancellation of certain harmonics does or does not occur.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The new API RP 500B-one year later
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: In 1985 an API (American Petroleum Institute) task committee, from a cross section of the oil-producing business, was formed to update API recommended practice (RP) 500B-Classification of Locations for Electrical Installations at Drilling Rigs and Production Facilities on Land and on Marine Fixed and Mobile Platforms, published in July 1973. The two-year effort culminated in the API release of the third edition of RP 500B on October 1, 1987. The authors present the engineering decisions made by the task group that were incorporated into the new RP 500B, and the effect this document has had on the industry a year after publication.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Technological advancement in self-limiting electric heat tracing cables
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: Self-limiting heating cable designs utilizing polycrystalline power disc technology are presented. These cables are capable of delivering a wide range of wattages for process applications, limiting their output using changes in temperature. The construction characteristics, qualifications, installation, and operating characteristics of polycrystalline power disc cables are examined. The cables' output is not substantially affected by applied voltage or by exposure to temperatures up to the temperature rating of their electrical insulation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The steps to select a high horsepower variable frequency fan drive system
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: A method for evaluating an application for a high horsepower variable-frequency fan drive is discussed, whose steps include selection of the flow control method, simulation of the fan and system load line, definition of the fan shaft power, component selection, a harmonic and torsional analysis, and an economic evaluation. These steps are illustrated for a pair of 5000 hp blowers at the BASF plant in South Kerney, New Jersey.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of a 40 year design life severe duty motor
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: In the development of a 40-yr live motor design, the factors that lead to motor failure are considered. An analysis of those components most affected is given, including consideration of enclosure, rotating elements, electrical winding, materials, and the manufacturing processes. It is concluded that since the winding is the heart of an electric motor, the selection of proper insulation to protect the winding from premature failure is essential.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On-line rectifier analyzer end user experiences
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: An online rectifier analyzer (OLRA) is described that provides more accurate measurements of current-carrying capacity of diodes in large multiphase rectifiers than other methods. The OLRA is highly reliable and automatically records measurements made. The OLRA is compared with other methods of rectifier semiconductor measurements, and some examples of use experiences with the OLRA are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A PLC application for large motor monitoring
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: Application is described of a PLC (programmable logic controller) for the gathering of data from solid-state motor protective devices and displaying that information in a control room some distance away. The PLC logic programming and BASIC programming required to accomplish this display of information are described. Programming tools and techniques to aid the engineer in implementing such a system are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: NEC Article 725: requirement or loophole
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: It is argued that Article 725 is one of the less obvious but powerful sections of the National Electrical Code. This article covers remote-control, signaling, and power-limited circuits that are not an integral part of a device or appliance. The limitations imposed and the advantages provided by the section are discussed. Application in conjunction with hazardous environments is presented. The installation, application, and transient protection of communications cable for instrumentation circuits is outlined. It is concluded that use of power-limited circuits with intrinsically safe equipment significantly reduces the complexity and cost associated with hazardous environments and inexpensive communication cable can be used for power-limited controls. Direct burial cable makes possible excellent performance and wide bandwidth. Lightning and transient protection can be very effectively implemented. Installation is simple and reliable.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Integrated metering and protective relay systems-large drive motor applications
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: Fully microprocessor based multifunction protective relay systems, which can improve the quality of classical protection functions and reduce the cost per function, are discussed. The feasibility and reliability of such units is demonstrated through full-scale testing with saturated circuits and through operating experience with field installations. The author covers distribution fault records, relay performance with extremely saturated low-ratio circuits, and advanced methods of protecting high-inertia drive motors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: RMS digital trips offer increased accuracy and reliability advances in low voltage circuit breaker trip technology
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: The function of low voltage circuit breaker trip units, and the need for direct RMS (root mean square) overcurrent sensing of the sinusoidal and nonsinusoidal current wave, including percentage error analysis are reviewed. It is found that the application of digital microprocessor technology to achieve direct RMS sensing allows the true RMS (heating) protection of thermal-electromechanical trip units, along with the precise protection and coordination selectivity of solid-state trip. This direct RMS sensing provides accurate long-time and short-time overcurrent protection in power distribution systems with the increasing occurrence of nonsinusoidal currents.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Preparation of shielded metal clad cables for sealing in classified locations
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: A basic tutorial on electrical noise interference in cable and conduit systems is presented. The ways in which noise is coupled into electrical circuits, and methods of minimizing that coupling, are discussed. A procedure is presented that allows the user to maintain single-point grounding continuity for shielded cables, while fully meeting National Electric Code (NEC) requirements for proper sealing in classified areas.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Replacing PCB equipment at products pipeline facilities
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: A five-step plan is presented for the replacement of PCB (polychlorinated biphenyl) insulation used in electrical equipment. The steps involved are identifying: (1) where the PCBs are, in what equipment, and how much testing of equipment is required; (2) what Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) rules apply to this equipment; (3) whether the PCB equipment presently complies with EPA rules, specifically in its markings, records, notifications, and whether there is a future restriction; (4) what potential hazards exist with each piece of PCB equipment in case of a leak, rupture, or fire (internal or external), and what type of cleanup and disposal would be required if a mishap occurs; and (5) what it will take to completely remove the PCBs from the facility, and until complete removal is accomplished, what can be done to mitigate the consequences of a mishap.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A comparison of protocol conversion methods for the retrofit of SCADA systems
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: SCADA (supervisory control and data acquisition) system retrofits present a problem not generally encountered in control system retrofits. Specifically, the problem is that the new RTUs (remote terminal units) generally use a different communications protocol than that used by the old RTUs and the central MTU (master terminal unit, or host computer), necessitating some form of protocol translation. The authors examine solutions to this problem. They describe methods for translation at the RTU, protocol conversion in MTU software, or translation using either a front-end processor or an MTU coprocessor. No solution is recommended generally.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Update of harmonic standard IEEE-519: IEEE Recommended Practices and Requirements for Harmonic Control in Electric Power Systems
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: The authors present the changes in IEEE STD 519-1981, titled IEEE Guide for Harmonic Control and Reactive Compensation of Static Power Converters, that are to be made in 1988 as the result of a two-year review. The voltage distortion criteria in the 1981 edition could not be used to distribute among users, the ability of the utility system to absorb harmonic currents. This problem is addressed in the revision. There are now two criteria that are used to evaluate harmonic distortion. The first is a limitation in the harmonic current that a user can transmit into the utility system. The second criterion is the quality of the voltage that the utility must furnish the user. Examples of the application of the revised standard, which has been upgraded to a Recommended Practice, are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Safety considerations for the application, installation, operation and maintenance of industrial AC induction motors
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: Hazardous conditions that can cause serious damage to equipment and create unsafe conditions for personnel are identified. The scope of the work is limited to industrial AC induction motors, even though much of it is appropriate to other types of electrical motors. The types of conditions covered include environmental, mechanical, electrical, and other hazards. Solutions to these problems include mechanical guards, proper and adequate grounding, proper and adequate spacing, and testing.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optimum electrical system design for a modern chlor-alkali plant
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: Development of the electrical distribution systems for a modern chlor-alkali plant is described starting from the conceptual design stage and continuing through final equipment design. Emphasis is placed on the electrical utility interface, main plant substation, 13.8 kV distribution system, rectifier design and control, and DC bus design. Load flow, voltage regulation, and harmonic studies are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Determination of motor quality through routine electrical tests
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: Types of mechanical and electrical tests that can be performed on fully assembled motors are described. The associated benefits (along with the corresponding costs) of these tests, are identified. These tests are normally run to ensure the motor(s) will run and/or perform as specified when delivered to the job site. However, many of the tests can be run in response to existing onsite problems to isolate or identify the cause. Recommendations are given for 100-3000 hp motors and should be applied based on the nature of the application.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: 1987 ampacity tables: de-mystifying the myths and tutorial (conductor rating)
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: In 1987, a change was made in the National Electric Code method of calculating the ampacity rating of power conductors. A tutorial on the revised method, including the new tables to be used, is presented. The tutorial covers the history of ampacity calculation, demonstrates and explains the use of the Neher-McGrath method, and answers the fallacious objections that have been put forth regarding the method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application and use of inspection checklists for factory and field inspection of electrical equipment
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: The requirements for a proper inspection and testing program during the design, procurement, and installation phases of projects is discussed. Appropriate tests are described, examples of criteria for acceptance are given, and the benefits of this program are shown. First the author deals with the factory inspection and witness tests that should be performed on electrical equipment, and then he discusses field testing and checkout of equipment. Discovering any equipment defects at the earliest stage can improve project schedule performance markedly, and proper timing of onsite testing can ensure contractor performance, as well as to detect damage or errors in installation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Coordination of relays, reclosers, and sectionalizing fuses for overhead lines in the oil patch
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: The authors cover certain generalities and fundamentals of oil-patch distribution system coordination, and identify some of the specific items of analysis to be concerned with. Some concepts are proposed for solutions to the problems of obtaining protective device coordination between sectionalizing fuses, line reclosers, and feeder breakers, especially as related to upgrading existing substation and feeder line protection on medium-voltage power systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electrical fast transient tests: applications and limitations
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: Recent proposals advocate fast-transient tests demonstrating external overvoltage interference immunity. The test waveforms represent electrostatic discharge effects of reignitions occurring during switching sequences. The rationale for requiring the tests is based on the assumption that interfering transients generated by power circuit switching will couple into adjacent power or signal lines, and will then propagate toward susceptible equipment. The authors describe specific measurements conducted for two typical low-voltage power line configurations, namely, a three-conductor line in a steel conduit and a three-conductor cable with a nonmetallic jacket. An attenuation model is proposed that provides a tool for understanding the significance of the line parameters and extends the usefulness of results to general cases. The two line configurations and their models yield similar results for measurements and for computations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Integrating of utility distribution system into a refinery plant generation/distribution network at Unocal Los Angeles refinery
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: The authors discuss the installation of a 46 MW cogeneration plant and the conversion of a 34.5 kV utility distribution system to a refinery distribution system with an interconnection to the utility to export or import electrical power. The cogeneration plant will be base-loaded and will supply about two-thirds of the normal steam supply for the refinery. The electricity produced will supply refinery needs, and the excess will be wheeled to other loads in the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A comparison of static and dynamic short circuit analysis procedures
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: The authors examine the differences between static and dynamic short-circuit analyses by comparing the results of each for a specific industrial power system. The static method used is that of ANSI C37.XX, which essentially calculates short-circuit duties of static points of time. The dynamic method, which is data-intensive, calculates the value of short-circuit currents for any time from fault incidence. All system time constants are considered for each fault point, and the effects of prefault voltages, derived from load from studies, can also be considered. This algorithm is an order of magnitude more complex that the static one. It is found that static method is sufficiently accurate for the selection and specification of switchgear based on maximum available short-circuit duties.

articleTitle: Design, specification, purchase, and installation of SF/sub 6/ power circuit breakers to replace overdutied OCBs
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: Electrical utility improvements and plant expansions have the available short-circuit interrupting current up to, and in some cases over and above, the 25000 A, 1500 MVA interrupting rating of some of existing 35 kV oil circuit breakers (OCBs). The authors discuss the process of replacing these OCBs with sulphur hexafluoride (SF/sub 6/) breakers. They address the entire project from the discovery of the problem through the investigation, analysis, engineering, purchase, and installation phases.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Industrial power system automation: synergistic benefits of integrating protection, instrumentation and control
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
abstract: Microprocessor-based implementations of protection, instrumentation, and control systems, which offer many user benefits individually, are discussed. The authors focus on those synergistic benefits made available when these functions are effectively integrated through data communications. Various ways in which industrial power users may benefit through reduced energy costs, more efficient utilization of power distribution equipment, and improved power system reliability are explored.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Record of Conference Papers. Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference (IEEE Cat. No.88-CH2661-7)
publicationTitle: Record of Conference Papers., Industrial Applications Society 35th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference,
